detailed_description: The CORS Tester sends browser fetch requests to a target HTTP or HTTPS URL and shows the CORS-related response headers that are visible to the page. Enter a URL, choose a request method, adjust the Origin value, then run a preflight-style OPTIONS request and the selected actual request. The result panel shows whether the browser request succeeded, lists access-control headers when they are exposed, and summarizes whether CORS appears enabled for the response. Because requests are made from the browser, results can still be limited by browser CORS rules and network errors.
usage_steps: Enter the target HTTP or HTTPS URL.
Choose the request method to test.
Review or edit the Origin value.
Click Test CORS to run the OPTIONS check and the selected request.
Review the status summary and visible CORS response headers.
Use Load Example if you want a sample URL to test first.
usage_examples: Check whether a public API exposes Access-Control-Allow-Origin to browser requests.
Compare how GET and POST requests behave for the same endpoint.
Test a staging endpoint with the current site origin before wiring it into frontend code.
Use the visible error message to distinguish browser blocking from a successful CORS response.
